data.narrative:
Osaro is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Derik Pridmore and Michael Kahane that has raised $86.8M to date. The valuation analysis is anchored to a comparable universe of 3 same-stage private peers in Robotics & Manufacturing—Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity—supplemented by a broader set of 8 private robotics companies and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline of $87M and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B progression, yields an implied valuation of $165M. Peer-median analysis across the three identified comparables produces a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. The peer-median approach carries greater weight given the direct comparability of stage and sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $140M to $2.0B, with a median of $957M. This wide spread reflects material uncertainty around which comparable set most appropriately reflects Osaro's growth trajectory and market position. The stage-progression method implies materially lower value, suggesting either that capital efficiency at Osaro differs from peer norms or that subsequent rounds may face dilutive pressure. The peer-median approach, conversely, assumes Osaro's competitive positioning aligns with the sample cohort. Resolution of this discrepancy requires deeper analysis of unit economics, customer concentration, and revenue trajectory relative to peers.
